Dr.P.R.Jayathilakan, vs A.Narayanan, on 7 March, 2013
Daily Order

 
 

 

 
 Kerala State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission Vazhuthacaud,Thiruvananthapuram   First Appeal No. A/12/223 (Arisen out of Order Dated 15/12/2011 in Case No. CC/06/124 of District Trissur)   1. DR.P.R.JAYATHILAKAN RTD GOVT.CHIEF MEDICAL OFFICER,THRPAYAR JUNCTION.P.O,NATTIKA TRISSUR KERALA ...........Appellant(s) Versus 1. A.NARAYANAN ARIMBOOR HOUSE,MULLOOR.P.O,PARAPUR TRISSUR KERALA ...........Respondent(s)   BEFORE:     HON'ABLE MR. SRI.M.K.ABDULLA SONA PRESIDING MEMBER   PRESENT:   ORDER 

KERALA STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION 
 

VAZHUTHACAUD THIRUVANANTHAPURAM 
 

  
 

                            APPEAL NOS.223/12 & 264/12 
 

                    COMMON JUDGMENT DATED 7.3.2013 
 

   
 

(Appeal filed against the order    in CC No.124/06 on the file of CDRF,   Thrissur dated 15.12..2011) 
 

  
 

 PRESENT 
 

   
 

 SHRI.M.K.ABDULLA SONA                                     --  MEMBER

Dr.P.R.Jayathilakan,

Thrissur.
APPEAL NO.264/12
A.Narayanan, 
 

Arimboor House,                                                       --   APPELLANT 
 

Mulloor P.O, Parapur 
 

Thrissur. 
 

   (By Adv.S.Reghukumar) 
 

  
 

                    Vs. 
 

   
 

Dr.P.R.Jayathilakan, 
 

Pokkanchery House,                                          --   RESPONDENT 
 

  
 

Rtd.Govrnment Chief Medical Officer, 
 

Thriprayar Junction, P.O.Nattika 
 

Thrissur. 
 

      (by Adv.G.S.Kalkura) 
 

  
 

   
 

 COMMON JUDGMENT 
 

   
 

 SHRI.M.K.ABDULLA SONA,MEMBER
Both appeal prefers from the order passed by the CDRF, Thrissur in CC.No.124/06 dated 15.12.01.  The Appeal No.223/12,  the appellant is the opposite party prefers this appeal from the order passed by the forum below that the appellant/opposite party is directed to pay Rs.50,000/- as compensation with cost of Rs.1,000/- within 2 months from the date of receipt of copy of the order.  If the amount is not paid within the prescribed time,   the complainant would be entitled to get 12% interest for compensation amount from the day of order till the realization.
2.  The Appeal No.264/12 filed  by the appellant/complainant who prefers this order from the above order on the ground that he is not satisfied with the amount ordered by the forum below.  Hence he prays to enhance the amount of compensation and costs ordered by the forum below.
3. In brief, the complainant is a retired Government employee and the opposite party is a retired Govt. Ayurvedic Doctor who claims that he can cure any heart disease through Ayurveda treatment.  The complainant is a heart patient and on 27.12.03 he approached Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences and Angiogram  was taken.  As per the Angiogram report there are three blocks in the nerve system of the heart.  At that period he noticed one advertisement in Mathrubhumi Arogyamasika  about the treatment and claims of the opposite party/doctor.  He consulted with the opposite party/doctor and he was promised and offered 100% cure of the disease.  The treatment started on 1.1.04 and was under the treatment up to 21.8.05.  As per the direction of  opposite party, the complainant took medicines as per the strict instruction of the opposite party/doctor.  He was strictly followed the  "Pathyam" as per the instruction of the opposite party/doctor.  After 20 months of this treatment the complainant approached Kovai Medical Centre and Angiogram was taken.  As per the report there are three blocks in the nerve system of the heart as stated in earlier report.  Subsequently the Bypass surgery was conducted at Kovai Medical Centre and spent Rs.95,000/-.  The complainant had given Rs.57,800/- to the opposite party for the treatment.   But there was no effect as per advertisement and as per the consumption of the medicine which promised by the opposite party/doctor the 100% cure of the ailment.  Hence the complaint.
4. The opposite party filed written version and strongly contended that the complainant was a person  of 61 years of age and  on 27.12.03 he was advised for bypass surgery.  In order to avoid the same he had consulted the opposite party/doctor.  The treatment was started on 1.1.04 and the medicines and Yoga methods were prescribed.  During the course of the treatment by the opposite party/doctor there was no serious difficulties  to the complainant and no treatment was taken for the disease at any hospitals.  Only because of the treatment of the opposite party was happened.  There were so many people who were recovered from the disease due to the treatment of the opposite party.  There was no deficiency in service from the part of the opposite party.  Hence prays to dismiss the complaint.
5. The evidence consisted of the oral testimony of the complainant who examined as PW1 and marked Ext.P1 to P8.  On the other side Dr.Jayathilakan the opposite party/doctor was examined as RW1 and marked Ext.R1 book written by one Tony Chittatukulam.
6. The forum below heard both parties and appreciated the entire evidence adduced by both sides and taken a view that the opposite party/doctor who committed unfair trade practice through a misleading advertisement.  The  complainant is also entitled for compensation from the opposite party/doctor.  It is the case of the complainant that he is entitled to get back the treatment expenses occurred out of the treatment of the opposite party/doctor.  But he is not entitled to get the same because he has no case that the doctor did not treat him.  Even after the treatment to the recovery was there he is only entitled to get compensation.  In the result, the forum below passed the above mentioned impugned order.
7. On this day, this appeal came before this Commission for final hearing, the counsel for the appellant in Appeal 223/12  argued the appeal on the basis of the grounds of the appeal memorandum that the forum below failed to appreciate the fact that the complainant did not have any serious problems though in the period  he was under- going the treatment of the opposite party.  In his evidence, the complainant has admitted that he was under the treatment for diabetes from 1983 and for Hypertension  from  1994 onwards.  He has also admitted that he was consulting  cardiologist from 2003 onwards. He has also admitted that while he was going to AIMS  he was  having chest pain and suffocation while walking.  He has also admitted that he was advised by the doctor of AIMS to undergo bypass surgery and to avoid.      He has deposed that when he consulted   doctor Pai of AIMS and he is advised to undergo a bypass surgery immediately and his condition was very critical.  He has also deposed that one tablet for B.P and one for avoiding blood clot was prescribed to him and during the long 20 months he was undergone the treatment of the opposite party and he was not using it as per the opposite parties advise.  He was not consulting any other doctor  during this period.  That means he was very good improvement due to the treatment and medicines given by the respondent and that is why he did not have any chest pain or heart attack during this period.  If the treatment of the opposite party   was not having any effect in his cardiac problems he would have suffered from a heart attack.
8. The counsel for the appellant submitted that the order passed by the forum below is not accordance with the provisions of law and evidence.  The appellant/opposite party doctor prescribed the Ayurvedic treatment and medicine.  All the Ayurvedic treatments on strict "Pathyam"  want to be followed.  In this case the respondent/complainant is 61 years old man and his cardiac problem was reduced due to the treatment of the appellant/opposite party doctor.   Another contention of the appellant/opposite party is that the patient/respondent did not approach to the appellant/doctor before he met with the Kovai Medical Centre and decided to undergo bypass surgery.  The counsel for the appellant prays to allow this appeal and also to set aside the impugned order passed by the forum below.  But the counsel for the appellant in Appeal No.264/12 is vehemently argued on the grounds of appeal memorandum that the respondent opposite party doctor who really misled the complainant through given vide publicity in his medicines and treatment.   The appellant who was attracted by an article in  Mathrubhumi Arogya Masika  regarding the complete cure of block in  Artery without surgery which promised by him to meet the opposite party. On this occasion the consul    submitted that the opposite party  doctor who was given an assurance to the complainant    about a complete  cure of the heart ailment. This is 100% guarantee.  The complainant undertook 20 months treatment from 1.1.2004 to 21.8.05.  The complainant who blindly believed the opposite party doctor  and he taken the treatment from him and also the complainant who taken the medicine which given by the doctor and he followed strictly  the Pathyam and other medical  instructions and conditions prescribed   by the opposite party doctor.  But even after he must undergone a bypass surgery on 1.9.09  at Kovai Medical Centre and he  had to incur an expense of Rs.95,000/- for his bypass surgery.  The bypass surgery is  nothing but a violation of the promise  assured  by the opposite party doctor.  It is deficiency in service.  At the very same time he is also attracted this treatment and medicine by reading  the Mathrubhumi Arogya Masika and a book  marked as Ext.R1.  The appellant is having a grievance that the forum below only ordered a compensation of Rs.50,000/- and cost of Rs,1000/-.  But  he spent Rs.95,000/- only for the bypass surgery.  Even after he spent money for purchasing the medicine and the treatment of Rs.57,800/- as a treatment expense.  He paid the money  not as a charity but a fee and expense for the magic remedy which offered by the opposite party doctor ")pAXDU`=\BT,^    The counsel for the appellant prays that the complainant approached to the Kovai Medical centre is a exclusively for the safeguard of his life.    He pull on the days with his heart ailment on the bonafidi belief that it will be cured through the promises treatment  given by the opposite party doctor.   Suppose he was waiting for that treatment, the result may be the death of the appellant/complainant.  The act of the opposite party is nothing but a  gross negligence and carelessness which resulted to a deficiency in service and unfair trade practice as per the provisions of the
Consumer Protection Act
.  The counsel for the appellant prays to enhance the compensation and cost ordered by the forum below on the basis of the solid evidence he adduced before the forum below.      The appellant prays to allow this appeal and also to enhance the compensation to Rs.5 lakhs and also to dismiss the Appeal No.223/12 which filed by the opposite party.
9. This Commission heard both sides in detail.  As per the evidence adduced by both sides, it is seeing that the opposite party doctor who is the appellant in 223/12 who committed gross negligence and unfair trade practice towards the respondent/complainant who is the appellant in Appeal No.264/12.  The complainant who taken the article published in Mathrubhumi Arogya Masika and  the book (Ext.R1) regarding the magic remedy  promised by the doctor Jayathilakan the opposite party.  The complainant taken his version    equal to the words of "The God."   There is nothing  wrong with this 100% assurance   and undergone the treatment of the opposite party by the complainant.  The opposite party doctor who is a retired Ayurvedic Physician  he is qualified in this subject and Government Ayurvedic doctor who is a member of the legally constituted  council of   the   Alternative Medical practitioners.    As per the professional ethics,  he cannot   publish in such a type of  advertisements both in the print and the electronic media.  He is definitely violated he professional ethics.  The complainant who was falsely  gained impression that the opposite party is a scholar in "Ashtanga Hridaya" and other traditional Ayurvedic Cardiac treatments.   The complainant approached to  him for avail this result oriented  treatment.  For such a treatment and remedy he spent Rs.57,800/-   under the impression that the entire heart ailment disease will be cured if he will be consumed the medicines given by the  opposite party doctor including obey the "Pathyams".  Then also undergone the treatment "prescribed by him" but the result is nothing but the complainant who suffered very   serious heart ailment then he must undergone bypass surgery.  It is not only unfair trade practice but also on deficiency in service.  But the arguments focused by the counsel for the appellant/opposite party such as the appellant/complainant who undergone the bypass un-necessarily and without met with the appellant/opposite party doctor is baseless and contempted.  According to the opposite party doctor, suppose the patient who approached to the opposite party doctor the complainant is need not conduct a bypass surgery.  It is nothing but an arrogant manner of defense  taken by the opposite party doctor.  The complainant who ignored the treatment and other assurances given by the Ayurvedic Physician   and he directly approached to Kovai Medical Centre which was the only reason to save and protect his life.  Suppose a doctor who is advertising in such a manner  and give  an   assurance of total cure of heart disease is beyond the control of any reputed genuine member of the medical profession in the world  in any branch of medicine.   Life is a gift of  "The God" and "The god can only capable to protect and save the life"  without the will of the God    nobody can save the life of any person  it is a  true fact.     But all the doctors are the deputers or the representatives of the God.  The God depute some persons to heal the disease of his fellowmen in certain extent.  It does not mean he is The  God.   In Greac Mythology a doctor is most blessed man.  Suppose such glorified persons are misused their holly duty is definitely contempt and ridiculous.    The advertisement is totally misleading and unfair trade practice.  The bypass surgery of the complainant is nothing but a violation of the terms, conditions  and assurance given by the opposite party doctor.  It is deficiency in service as per the provisions of the
Consumer Protection Act
.  This Commission examined each and every piece of the evidence adduced by both sides and heard both sides in very detail.
10.
In the decision of the apex court  "Cuajash Hospital (Private Limited) Vs. Prasannakumar Ojsh (2) 2003 2 CPJ 150 (NC) and in   another decision
Poonam Varma Vs. Doctor Aswin Patel
1995 (1)  CPJ (NC)   in a decision,
India Medical Association Vs. V.P.Santha
1995 (6) SC 651 .  The Hon.Supreme Court held that as per the law, under which a medical practitioner who was registered as a medical practitioner   required him  to practice in Homoeopathy only he was under a statutory  duty not to enter   the field  of any other system of medicine as, admittedly, he was not qualified in other system, Alopathy to be precise.  He trespassed into a prohibited field and was liable to be prosecuted  under
Section 15 (3)
of the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.  A person who does not have knowledge of a particular system of medicine but practices in that system is a "quake" and a mere pretender to medical knowledge or skill or to put it differently on charlatm.
His conduct amount to an actionable  negligence particularly  as a duty of the care indicate by the Supreme Court in Dr.Lakshman Joshi case.
11. This Commission heard both sides in very detail.  It is seeing that the order passed by the forum below is strictly  accordance with the provisions of law and evidence.  It is legally sustainable.  This Commission is not seeing any reason to interfere in the impugned order passed by the forum below.  This omission is uphold the order passed by the forum below except the result portion of the order passed by the forum below/.  This Commission decide to dismiss the Appeal No.223/12 which filed by the opposite party doctor without cost but the Appeal No.264/12  which filed by the appellant/complainant is allowed in part.
12.          In the result, Appeal No.223/12 which filed by the appellant/opposite party is dismissed and Appeal No.264/12 by the appellant/complainant is allowed in part.  The result portion of the order passed by the forum below is modified and  enhanced the compensation as Rs.95,000/- instead of Rs.50,000/- and enhance the cost of Rs.2,500/- instead of Rs.1000/- accordingly.  The opposite party is directed to pay Rs.95,000/-,  under the head of the treatment expenses spent by the complainant for  the heart surgery of  the complainant along with cost of Rs.2,500/- to the complainant by the opposite party within one month from the date of receipt of copy of this order.   If the amount is not paid within the stipulated time, the complainant is entitled to get 15% interest on the entire amount  ordered in this appeal from the date of filing the appeal till the date of the realization.  Other portions  of the order except the result portion passed by the forum below is confirmed.  These appeals are disposed accordingly.  No separate cost ordered.
The Registrar of this Commission is directed to forward a copy of this Judgment to the Travancore Cochin Medical Council, Thiruvananthapuram for alternative medical practitioners  for taking necessary disciplinary action against the appellant doctor P.R.Jayathilakan for the violation of the professional ethics if any and is direct to report to this Commission within 6 months.  The disobedience of the order passed by this Commission is liable for imprisonment a period of 3 years and fine Rs.10,000/- both as per
Section 27
of the Consumer Protection Act, 2003 Amendment Act.
M.K.ABDULLA SONA   --  MEMBER
